newsitem.title: DENMARK: NatWest analyst sees SAS 40 pct up in year.
newsitem.headline: NatWest analyst sees SAS 40 pct up in year.

text.p: Britain's NatWest transport analyst predicted on Thursday that Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) shares would rise 40 percent in the next year.

"SAS is the most undervalued aviation share in Europe. Many people think that the airline is losing market shares to low-cost airlines but it is my impression that SAS is winning against them at the moment," analyst Mike Powell told Reuters by telephone from London.
He was speaking on Thursday afternoon when SAS shares had already surged to 95-96 crowns. The shares closed at 97 crowns, up 7.00 crowns or 7.8 percent from Wednesday's close.
SAS, jointly owned by the governments of Denmark, Sweden and Norway and private investors, forecasts 1997 full year pre-tax profits on par with last year's 1.8 billion Swedish crowns.
This is despite a first quarter 1997 loss of 269 million crowns and increasing competition on home markets from cut-price operators since deregulation opened Scandinavian skies.
